scenarios.name: Lexically supported Spanish rejects non-topical speech
scenarios.given: Spanish lexical tagging is available on the device
scenarios.when: History content eligibility checks filler, a generic decision query and real topic content
scenarios.then: filler and generic queries are insufficient while topic passages and short topical queries remain eligible

scenarios.name: Unavailable lexical tagging remains unknown
scenarios.given: a language does not advertise lexical tagging on the current runtime
scenarios.when: filler or topic text is checked for History content eligibility
scenarios.then: neither fallback OtherWord tags nor missing tags are treated as known noun evidence; eligibility stays unknown

scenarios.name: Existing English content rules remain intact
scenarios.given: English lexical tagging is available and language may be explicit or detected
scenarios.then: existing generic meeting nouns and vague queries are insufficient, topic nouns remain eligible and empty text is insufficient

scenarios.name: Unhinted single-word queries do not lose compatible model routing
scenarios.given: a short History query has one word and no explicit language hint
scenarios.when: language or lexical tagging could assign that word different meanings across languages
scenarios.then: content eligibility remains unknown without requiring installed lexical assets, so the query can reach compatible stored models

scenarios.name: Explicit language and multiword queries retain native Spanish policy
scenarios.given: Spanish lexical tagging is installed on the native Mac test host
scenarios.when: a topical one-word query, a non-topical explicit-language word and an unhinted multiword decision query are checked
scenarios.then: the topical query stays eligible while the other two queries remain insufficient; short-query independence does not bypass explicit lexical evidence
